item.content:encoded:
The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start.
Specifically since August 17, he's been one of the best hitters in all of baseball. He leads the Los Angeles Dodgers in all three triple-slash categories (.336/.427/.611), wRC+ (183), home runs (seven), RBI (27), and fWAR (2.0) from that point forward, emerging at a time when the team has gotten all of 71 plate appearances (and a 101 wRC+) from Shohei Ohtani.
Betts isn't a "secret weapon" by traditional standards; his MVP credentials and three World Series rings would certainly beg to differ. But after he struggled mightily a year ago and then followed that up with an even worse encore at the beginning of 2026, having him healthy and in his best groove in years could be the deciding factor in the Dodgers' quest for a three-peat.
Mookie Betts has elevated his own floor and with it, the Dodgers' ceiling
The Dodgers are hardly hurting for production, ranking third in the league in runs scored since mid-August. Even without Ohtani, they can batter opposing pitching staffs with their depth, especially now that Kyle Tucker finally looks interested in participating in this group project.
But more than a rejuvenated Tucker or red-hot Teoscar Hernández, there's something special about Betts in particular getting this hot. He's the fourth-longest tenured player on the roster, surpassed by only Max Muncy and Will Smith among position players. He's been around for each of the three recent championships, posting a cumulative OPS over .800 in those playoff runs.
One of the most selfless superstars you'll ever find, there's a "you go, we go" aura that orbits Betts, especially now that he's reclaimed his rightful spot atop the batting order as Dave Roberts' leadoff hitter. His all-around talents lengthen the lineup to a tremendous degree, something opposing pitchers will really feel once Ohtani is back in the fold.
It's not all perfect, of course. His hard-hit rate even during this hot streak is well below the figures he'd post in his prime, and he's still hitting a few too many balls on the ground. Naturally, all of his expected stats during this stretch fall shy of his actual results, including significant disparities in his slugging percentage (.611 compared to a .458 xSLG) and wOBA (.443 compared to a .374 xwOBA).
Those expected metrics are still leaps and bounds better than we got earlier this season, though, and that's the real takeaway here. Even if Betts can't keep this MVP-caliber charade going through all of October, he's clearly found a more stable baseline level of performance that can still help the Dodgers win.

item.title: [fansided.com] MLB Power Rankings: Playoff stakes rise as October contenders make their move
item.dc:creator: Chris Landers; Mark Powell
item.description: The playoffs technically don't start for another week or so, but good luck telling that to teams for which every game already feels like October. With the standings in both the NL and AL as jumbled as they've been in recent memory, the stakes are already as high as can be — and whoever gets hot now could well ride that wave all the way to a World Series. "Hot" could definitely describe both the San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians of late. The former has decided to just never lose again, not
item.content:encoded:
The playoffs technically don't start for another week or so, but good luck telling that to teams for which every game already feels like October. With the standings in both the NL and AL as jumbled as they've been in recent memory, the stakes are already as high as can be — and whoever gets hot now could well ride that wave all the way to a World Series.
"Hot" could definitely describe both the San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians of late. The former has decided to just never lose again, not only grabbing hold of a Wild Card spot but now pushing for home-field in the first round if things break right. The latter, meanwhile, has once again snatched the AL Central while no one was looking. And they're not the only ones making serious moves in our latest MLB power rankings.
But who are we buying as serious title contenders, and who still has work to do? Read on to find out.
30. Colorado Rockies
The Rockies have admittedly let go of the rope of late, well on their way to yet another 100-loss season. There are at least some promising young hitters in this organization, which represents something to build upon moving forward. Of course, the pitching staff remains a mess, and no one's been able to crack that nut yet in Colorado.
–Chris Landers, FanSided.com editor
29. Los Angeles Angels
In Reid Detmers, Walbert Urena and Ryan Johnson, the Angels have at least some sort of foundation upon which to build for the future. Well, OK, maybe not Detmers, who will almost certainly be dealt this offseason. But still, L.A.’s pitching staff has been a real bright spot of late. The offense … well, that’s another question. Things are going to get worse before they get better under John Mozeliak. At least Arte Moreno is no longer around to meddle in it.
–CL
28. Athletics
The A’s are playing out the string of a lost season, although the contributions they’ve gotten from young bats like Henry Bolte, Max Muncy (not that one), Lawrence Butler and Zack Gelof down the stretch have been notable. None of that will matter, though, until the team fixes its pitching staff. We know we sound like a broken record, but it really is that simple, and no potential answers have emerged in the second half.
–CL
27. San Francisco Giants
Rafael Devers' injury, which figures to cost him at least some of next season as well as the end of this one, is a fitting if unfortunate end to what's been a miserable season by the Bay. Devers had been one of the few bright spots on this Giants team down the stretch alongside Bryce Eldridge; now, it's unclear how San Francisco will rebuilt its offense for 2027 in addition to finding reinforcements for a pitching staff that simply hasn't been good enough.
–CL
26. Kansas City Royals
The Kansas City Royals have been eliminated for quite some time now. If there is one clear goal for Kansas City this winter, it's to build a roster around Bobby Witt Jr. that is capable of making a postseason run. That is every team's goal, but the Royals are so far away from contention despite featuring such a prolific player, Witt Jr.'s career is closer to becoming Mike Trout's than Derek Jeter's.
-Mark Powell, FanSided.com MLB director
25. Minnesota Twins
At one point not all that long ago, the Twins had a realistic chance to make the playoffs as the third AL Wild Card spot. Then, the bottom fell out. Byron Buxton underwent successful hip surgery just last week that will keep him out until spring training, whenever that may be. The Twins once again experienced the roster flaw of building around an injured star.
-MP
24. New York Mets
This week couldn’t have been more awkward for the New York Mets when Pete Alonso hit his 300th home run in his return to Citi Field, much to the delight of many Mets fans in attendance, but once Alonso left town, the Mets began to play better, winning two games in a row against the Phillies. Those wins, headlined by more quality play from youngsters like Carson Benge, Zac Thornton and Christian Scott, show why Mets fans should be somewhat enthusiastic for what’s to come.
–Zach Rotman, FanSided.com staff writer
23. Cincinnati Reds
In the American League, the Reds likely wouldn't be the worst team in their division. But the NL Central has been a gauntlet all year long, and the Reds couldn't keep up. Despite breakthrough seasons from Elly De La Cruz and Sal Stewart, Cincinnati still has a long way to go on the starting pitching front. Can they rely on Hunter Greene and Chase Burns moving forward?
-MP
22. Seattle Mariners
Going 3-3 against the Angels and Rockies this week just about sums up this season in Seattle. The good news is that youngsters like Michael Arroyo and Lazaro Montes have helped to key an offensive turnaround. The bad news is that the starting rotation hasn’t held up its end of the bargain of late, and there are still tons of long-term questions about this lineup — especially with Randy Arozarena set to hit free agency. Jerry DiPoto will need to find some answers this offseason after a year in which just about everything went wrong.
–CL
21. Washington Nationals
The Washington Nationals deserved a better fate in 2026. Even with their offense falling off a bit of late, they’re still third in the majors in runs scored. The dynamic duo of CJ Abrams and James Wood is as good as any in the National League. Recently extended Cade Cavalli is a budding ace. Andrew Alvarez has thrown the ball incredibly well and looks like a future rotation stalwart. If it weren’t for a historically bad bullpen, we’d be talking about this team in Wild Card contention.
–ZR
20. Detroit Tigers
The Tigers have the best run differential in the AL Central and a pythagorean record of an AL playoff team. None of it matters. Scott Harris and the Tigers front office gave up on their team's postseason hopes at the trade deadline. Then, they proceeded to get fans' hopes up with a late August run, only to play like the team Harris assumed they'd become when it mattered most. The Tigers have some work to do, though the emergence of young stars in the lineup like Hao-Yu Lee and Kevin McGonigle, paired with Riley Greene's consistent play, give them some building blocks.
-MP
19. St. Louis Cardinals
The Cardinals are ahead of schedule, but not a postseason team. Make no mistake about it, St. Louis came crashing back down to earth in September, and has been eliminated from playoff contention. There are questions about the long-term future of Masyn Winn, especially with JJ Wetherholt as the de-facto shortstop of the future. But these are all good problems to have. Now, if only Bloom could find an ace burried in that farm system of his.
-MP
18. Baltimore Orioles
A series against league-best Milwaukee came at the worst possible time for the O’s, which now find themselves needing to hit an inside straight to snatch the final Wild Card spot. Pete Alonso’s heroics at Citi Field aside, Baltimore’s bats simply have not been good enough. Heck, no part of this team has; they’re hovering around .500 for a reason, after all, and there’s no reason to think they have the consistency required to get hot over the final week and overtake the White Sox, Blue Jays and Astros.
–CL
17. Miami Marlins
The Miami Marlins tried to do what they could to stick around in the NL postseason hunt, even using Sandy Alcantara on one day of rest in a save opportunity, but they were eliminated following Friday’s loss in San Diego. As disappointing as that is, the Marlins could finish above .500 for just the third time since 2009. That’s a sign that things are heading in the right direction for Miami.
–ZR
16. Toronto Blue Jays
The Jays have lost three of four series now, and news that Dylan Cease will have his next start bumped due to shoulder fatigue makes it even less likely that Toronto can sneak its way into the playoffs. With Trey Yesavage and Shane Bieber already on the IL, the rotation has begun leaking oil, and that’s not something this power-starved lineup is equipped to handle. The Jays still have a path to the final Wild Card spot, but it’s becoming an increasingly tenuous one, and it’s hard to see them making much noise even if they did get in.
–CL
15. Houston Astros
Getting swept at home by the Braves this weekend might well wind up costing the Astros a playoff spot. The closing schedule isn’t too tough, with trips to Seattle and Sacramento on tap. Still, if Houston doesn’t figure out where its high-powered offense went before it’s too late — and if Joe Espada can’t stop his bullpen from blowing late leads — Yordan Alvarez’s MVP season may well be for nought. As it stands, this looks like a team with fatal flaws that will spoil what could have been a deep run in a wide-open AL.
–CL
14. Chicago White Sox
Reality hit the White Sox real quick. Chicago has lingered around .500 for longer than they'd care to admit, and it was only a matter of time before the rest of the Central caught up to them. Munetaka Murakami has been dreadful since the trade deadline, and thus any contract extension talks have been put on hold. If the White Sox can hold on to a playoff spot, they'll be one of the best stories in October. If not, this season could all be for naught.
-MP
13. Texas Rangers
All of a sudden, the Rangers find themselves back in control of the AL West and home-field advantage in the first round of the playoffs. Of course, that says more about the West than it does about Texas; this is still a .500 team, one without a ton of depth on either side of the ball. The interesting thing, though, is that this lineup has finally started to show signs of life of late. Take care of business against the Twins and Mets this week, and no one’s going to want to face a team with Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi in the rotation plus an offense featuring Corey Seager, Wyatt Langford and Josh Jung.
-CL
12. Pittsburgh Pirates
The narrative Pirates fans are spinning these days is the same web every National League non-playoff team will get caught in this week; if only we played in the American League! Yes, the disparity between leagues is easy to blame for the Pirates shortcomings, but the front office also fell short in acquiring bullpen arms last winter, which could've kept Pittsburgh from blowing an extraordinary number of leads in the season's first half. That'll haunt these Pirates forever.
-MP
11. Arizona Diamondbacks
It's not Arizona's fault that their primary competition for a Wild Card spot, San Diego, has become one of the hottest teams in baseball over the last few weeks. Either way, though, Arizona has simply run out of bullets, especially in a rotation that hasn't gotten the boost from Corbin Burnes' return that they were hoping for. Eduardo Rodriguez has turned back into a pumpkin, and there's just not enough depth to keep pace with what's become a beast of an NL playoff chase.
–CL
10. Cleveland Guardians
Here we go again with the Guardians. Cleveland is a legitimate threat in a weak American League. Much like last season, the Guards are taking advantage of a fellow contender floundering down the stretch. This is when Cleveland plays its best baseball, so it should be no surprise they've won five straight games heading into Monday's potential postseason preview against the Red Sox.
-MP
9. Boston Red Sox
Dropping consecutive series to the Rangers and Rays won’t do much to Boston’s postseason outlook — they’ve been more or less locked into a Wild Card series in the Bronx for a while now — but it still doesn’t inspire confidence in this team’s ability to make a run come October. This offense is once again mired in a power outage, and while getting Willson Contreras and others back from the IL figures to help, who knows when that might actually be. And there’s still just a real dearth of power here that even this pitching staff might not be able to make up for.
–CL
8. Philadelphia Phillies
I don’t know what to think of the Philadelphia Phillies. On one hand, a rotation led by Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sanchez, a healthy Jesus Luzardo, a rejuvenated Aaron Nola and a much-improved Andrew Painter should will them to wins. On the other hand, Luzardo is not healthy, the lineup is top-heavy and the bullpen, outside of Jhoan Duran, is an utter disaster. The Phillies are almost certainly going to make the playoffs, but their losses in New York this week ruined any last hope they had at a division title. And with how they’re playing right now, I don’t know if I’d pick them to get beyond the Wild Card Round.
–ZR
7. Chicago Cubs
The Cubs playoff parade was put on hold Sunday as Alex Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball. Bregman was taken to the local hospital, and it's unclear how much time he will miss as of this writing. Chicago's postseason hopes may hang in the balance, as their one clear advantage over every other NL team is their lineup. The Cubs have scored the most runs in baseball this year.
-MP
6. San Diego Padres
Yes, the schedule has helped, particularly series against Miami, Colorado, Washington, San Francisco and Cincinnati. But no matter who they've played, the Padres look like a different team from the one we saw for much of the year, with their big bats finally mashing and their rotation coming into focus with Nick Pivetta now back in the fold. San Diego is now dead even with Chicago and Philly in the Wild Card race, and no one will want to face this lineup and this bullpen in a short series.
–CL
5. New York Yankees
Just when it seemed like New York was getting ready to make a move, with Aaron Judge finally back in the lineup after months on the shelf, the reigning AL MVP landed right back on the IL — this time with a calf strain that could well jeopardize his entire postseason. It’s been that sort of year for the Yankees, which have the pitching to keep believing in them as contenders but just haven’t been able to put it all together enough to take command of their own playoff destiny. And with a Judge-less offense and a penchant for mistake-filled baseball, winning three series in a row feels like a tough ask even in this AL.
–CL
4. Atlanta Braves
The Atlanta Braves punched their ticket to the playoffs this week, and thanks to the Phillies’ struggles, they’re on the cusp of winning the NL East — ensuring a top-three seed in the National League. Tyler Mahle pitched another gem, and Ronald Acuña Jr. is hitting his stride at the perfect time. There’re still some concerns with the team, like the No. 3 spot in their rotation and struggling stars like Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies, but getting to the playoffs is a big deal, and the Braves can take pride in checking that box.
–ZR
3. Tampa Bay Rays
The Rays may well have sewn up the AL East this week, taking two of three from the Red Sox over the weekend to stretch their lead over the Yankees ahead of an all-important four-game set in the Bronx beginning on Tuesday. Even if New York were to sweep all four, though, Tampa would still have the inside track to the division and the No. 1 overall seed. This pitching staff continues to thrive beyond all expectation even with some recent injuries, and the hitting has done just enough. Whether that recipe will withstand the postseason is the only question now.
–CL
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
Don't look now, but L.A.'s lineup has begun to stir, with Kyle Tucker looking like the player the Dodgers thought they were paying for this offseason. They also got Edwin Diaz back this week, and he's suddenly looking like the star closer of old — potentially answering this team's biggest question entering October. We know the rotation will be there; if they have Tucker at the height of his powers and a one-two punch in Diaz and Tanner Scott at the end of games, the three-peat march might be back on.
–CL
1. Milwaukee Brewers
The Brewers set a franchise record with 98 wins on Sunday. They still have a full week to go to add to that mark, and appear likely to reach the 100-win plateau. That's a great accomplishment, but it won't mean squat if Milwaukee falls to the Los Angeles Dodgers — or any other NL team for that matter — on their way to that elusive NL pennant. The Brewers are the favorites, but the Dodgers are lingering right behind them.
-MP

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants. They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.
Week 26 results
6-1 record
39 runs scored (5.57 per game)
16 runs allowed (2.29 per game)
.836 pythagorean win percentage
Year to date
96-60 record
780 runs scored (5.00 per game)
587 runs allowed (3.76 per game)
.627 pythagorean win percentage (98-58)
Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Josue De Paula responds to criticism about defense with bold prediction
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut. Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level. But his defense in the outfield is a m
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut.
Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level.
But his defense in the outfield is a major area of concern, and it’s part of the reason the Dodgers did not call De Paula up until needing a regular DH. As they look ahead to the postseason, De Paula is likely to be limited to being a bat off the bench, given his defensive struggles and the uptick of production from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker.
However, De Paula knows he needs to improve in the outfield, and he’s made it a focus during his first stint at the MLB level.
“Every day. I know that’s a big area of improvement for me, and I know I’ve got a lot of hate on it,” De Paula said. “I’m the type that if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. I’m going to shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.”
De Paula has spent time before every game practicing his defense, working with Dodgers coaches to become more of a usable option in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has taken notice of that, and issued a challenge to De Paula.
“Well, it’s clear he needs to improve on his defense,” Roberts said. “How do you shut people up? You perform better. You practice hard, and that’s how you do it. My challenge to him is to be a complete baseball player, and not just to be a hitter. So he’s putting a lot of good work with Dino every day, and so I welcome that.”
Josue De Paula praises Dodgers teammates
De Paula became the first position player promoted from Double-A by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, creating lofty expectations for himself.
The 21-year-old has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head-on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” De Paula said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”

It’s a chance to give him two days, then six in a
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Kyle Tucker didn’t start on Sunday, one day after fouling a ball off his right knee, but the Dodgers right fielder insisted that he felt fine. This was more of a chance to pair a rest day for Tucker with Monday’s scheduled off day for the team.
“[The off day] wasn’t planned. I just felt that after he took one off the knee, this would have been 10 in a row for him,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s playing well, played a lot. It’s a chance to give him two days, then six in a row to finish the season.”
The injury was in a much higher spot on his leg than the right shin fracture that cost him two months on the injured list during the 2024 season while with the Houston Astros.
Tucker did pinch-hit in the eighth inning on Sunday, and he’s second on the Dodgers in games played (148), starts (141), and plate appearances (602), trailing only Freddie Freeman in all three categories. Tucker is playing the best baseball of his season at the moment with five home runs in his last 10 starts, hitting .417/.500/.972 since September 9.
Notes
Speaking of playing in the outfield on Tuesday, the Dodgers will likely activate center fielder Andy Pages off the injured list to play in the series opener against the San Diego Padres, after he missed the last 27 games after a fastball broke his left hand on August 21.
Pages at the end of this season will have two years, 155 days of major league service time and will be eligible for salary arbitration for the first time as a Super Two player, among the top 70 percent in service time among major leaguers with two years but not yet three years of service time. MLB Trade Rumors last week projected the cutoff for Super Two players this offseason to be two years, 134 days.
Longtime Dodgers third base coach Joey Amalfitano and knuckleballer Charlie Hough were honored on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Sunday’s game as the 2026 winners of the the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award. This is the fifth year of the award, timed close to Lasorda’s birthday, which is Tuesday.

Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles llamaron de vuelta al lanzador Emmet Sheehan como parte de una serie de movimientos en el roster el domingo, y está previsto que el derecho se encargue de la mayor parte del juego en el cierre de la serie contra los Gigantes de San Francisco.
Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. También llamaron de vuelta a Kyle Hurt, colocaron a Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo y enviaron a Seth Halvorsen a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Movimientos en el roster de los Dodgers
Jack Dreyer abrirá mientras los Dodgers buscan la barrida ante sus rivales del Área de la Bahía, antes de cederle el turno a Sheehan.
"Hoy estamos armando esto un poco con las opciones disponibles. Creo que se trata más de lo que, en nuestra opinión, le da a Emmet la mejor oportunidad", comentó el mánager Dave Roberts.
El jardinero derecho Kyle Tucker no estará en la alineación después de salir de la victoria del sábado por 10-4 debido a un lanzamiento foul que le pegó en la rodilla derecha.
Lesiones y esperanzas de regreso
Los Dodgers esperan ver pronto de regreso a Shohei Ohtani tras su primera estancia en la lista de lesionados desde que se unió al equipo en 2024. Podría ocurrir durante una serie de tres juegos contra los San Diego Padres que comienza la noche del martes. "Aún está en el aire, pero esa es nuestra esperanza", señaló Roberts.
Ohtani está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho. También ha estado lidiando con molestias en la rodilla izquierda desde hace meses.
Expectativas sobre el regreso de Ohtani
Roberts cree que Ohtani llegará sin dolor a la última semana de la temporada regular, mientras los Dodgers presionan para asegurar un descanso y evitar la ronda de comodines.
"Creo que hay una diferencia entre molestia y dolor. ¿Está al 100 por ciento? Probablemente no. ¿Está mejor que hace una semana? Sí", manifestó Roberts.

item.title: [bozemandailychronicle.com] Dodgers recall Sheehan to face Giants, put Skubal on bereavement, hope to have Ohtani back soon
item.dc:creator: DAN GREENSPAN
item.description: LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled pitcher Emmet Sheehan as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with the right-hander set to handle the bulk of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants. All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled pitcher Emmet Sheehan as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with the right-hander set to handle the bulk of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way to Sheehan, who is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 games this season.
“Kind of piecing through the available options today,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I think it's just more of what gives Emmet, in our opinion, the best chance.”
Right fielder Kyle Tucker won't be in the lineup after coming out of Saturday's 10-4 victory because of a fouled pitch that went off his right knee. The early exit was described as precautionary, and Roberts felt it was worth giving him a day off, particularly with Tucker finding his stride after an erratic first season in Los Angeles. He is batting .429 with five homers, eight extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in his past 10 games.
The Dodgers expect to see Shohei Ohtani back soon after his first stint on the injured list since joining the team in 2024. It could come during a three-game series against the San Diego Padres that starts Tuesday night. “Still up in the air, but that’s our hope,” Roberts said.
Ohtani is on the 15-day IL with right biceps inflammation. He also has been dealing with left knee soreness for months.
Roberts believes Ohtani will be pain-free going into the last week of the regular season, with the Dodgers pushing to secure a bye to avoid the wild-card round.
“I think there's a difference between discomfort and pain,” Roberts said. “Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes. Honestly, I think that's just a better question for Shohei to give specifics. But I do think that when he's activated, it's going to be the best physical place he's been in in quite some time.”

item.description: Kyle Tucker has started to heat up at the perfect time for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Signed this past offseason to a massive four-year, $240 million deal, he spent most of the summer struggling at the plate and unable to string together any consistent production. item.content:encoded:
Kyle Tucker has started to heat up at the perfect time for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Signed this past offseason to a massive four-year, $240 million deal, he spent most of the summer struggling at the plate and unable to string together any consistent production. Just when it seemed like he would get hot, he would slide right back into another cold stretch.
However, September has been a different story entirely for Tucker. Over 18 games this month, the 29-year-old has posted a .288 batting average, .397 on-base percentage, 1.075 OPS, six home runs and 13 RBIs, while striking out just seven times and walking 12. The discipline and production have both been at an elite level.
The Dodgers are on the verge of clinching a first-round bye in the National League, and Tucker's surge has undoubtedly been a big reason why.
During Saturday's win against the San Francisco Giants, Tucker fouled a ball off his right shin and appeared to be in some discomfort. He remained in the game and finished it, and manager Dave Roberts said afterward he did not expect it to be an issue moving forward.
However, Tucker was not included in Sunday's series finale lineup against San Francisco. Teoscar Hernandez shifted to right field with Enrique Hernandez taking over the vacated spot in left field.
Speaking with reporters pregame, Tucker continued to downplay the issue and revealed he did not undergo any further testing. "I feel fine," Tucker said, per Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic.
Kyle Tucker: “I feel fine.”
Said he didn’t get any further testing. Like he said yesterday, hit him on a different spot than where he broke his shin in 2024. https://t.co/8KvewI1fkA
Tucker has an injury history with his right shin, previously breaking it back in 2024 when he was with the Houston Astros.
However, this situation is nowhere near as serious, and he will look to return for Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres. It is unclear if he will be available off the bench Sunday.

Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen.
The Dodgers also gave right fielder Kyle Tucker Sunday off after he fouled a ball off the lower knee/upper shin area on his right leg on Saturday night. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness will become an ongoing issue for Tucker, who is expected back in the lineup on Tuesday.
Here's how these moves will impact the Dodgers on Sunday and beyond:
Skubal will be away from the team for "a couple days," Roberts said. Players may spend between three to seven days on the bereavement list, so Skubal might not miss his next start, which is projected to come on Friday in San Francisco.
"Some personal stuff going on," Roberts said, "but he's fine."
Skubal is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts since being dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline.
Sheehan was set to pitch bulk innings on Sunday behind opener Jack Dreyer. The thought was that pitching Sheehan behind an opener could not only help him get deeper into the game, but also prepare him for a possible bullpen role in the postseason, which would be his only path to making the roster.
In his previous two starts for the Dodgers, Sheehan allowed one earned run across 11 2/3 innings. After a strong stint in Triple-A, he has looked to trend in the right direction in what has been an inconsistent season overall (5-8, 4.79 ERA).
Tucker has heated up at the end of the first season of his four-year, $240 million contract, which has been disappointing (his .728 OPS is on track to be a career-worst mark in a full season). Since Sept. 9, he's hitting 15-for-35 (.429) with five home runs and 35 total bases, his most in a 10-game span this season.
On Saturday, Tucker exited the game after six innings due to a combination of the hit-by-pitch and the lopsided score. He said he feels fine, but Roberts decided to give him an extra day to rest after Tucker had played the previous nine games without a day off.
"I feel like everyone's grinding at this point in the season," Tucker said. "But I'll be good with it."

item.title: [New York Post] Kyle Tucker out of Dodgers lineup as new injury concern surfaces
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Just as Kyle Tucker was finally starting to heat up, he became the latest Dodgers star to suffer a potential injury concern. On Sunday, Tucker was not in the Dodgers’ lineup for their series-finale against the San Francisco Giants, absent a day after he left Saturday’s game early following a foul ball off his right knee/shin area. The good news: Tucker insisted on Sunday that he felt fine and didn’t anticipate it causing ongoing problems. Still, manager Dave Roberts had said Saturday night he ex
item.content:encoded:
Just as Kyle Tucker was finally starting to heat up, he became the latest Dodgers star to suffer a potential injury concern.
On Sunday, Tucker was not in the Dodgers’ lineup for their series-finale against the San Francisco Giants, absent a day after he left Saturday’s game early following a foul ball off his right knee/shin area.
The good news: Tucker insisted on Sunday that he felt fine and didn’t anticipate it causing ongoing problems.
Still, manager Dave Roberts had said Saturday night he expected Tucker in the lineup on Sunday, depending on how the issue progressed.
Tucker initially suffered the injury in the third inning Saturday night, when a foul ball banged high enough up his leg it evaded his shin pad.
The four-time All-Star immediately went down in pain, and was checked out by Roberts and a trainer for several moments.
Initially, Tucker stayed in the game, drawing a walk (and racing around the bases to later score a run) in the fifth while playing out in right field until the seventh.
However, he appeared to be moving around somewhat gingerly after the injury, and was ultimately removed once the score got out of reach in the Dodgers’ eventual 10-4 win.
Postgame, Tucker didn’t seem overly concerned with the issue, saying he should be “good with it” and that the lopsided score was a factor in his precautionary removal.
“I feel like everyone is grinding at this point of the season,” he noted.
On Sunday morning, he echoed that sentiment, saying Roberts had informed him Sunday they were “just gonna at least give me the day.”
The Dodgers will have to hope the injury doesn’t impact Tucker’s recently resurgent performance. In his last 10 games, the $240 million outfielder has finally started to turn a corner, going 15-for-35 with five home runs, nine extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in that stretch.
In 2024, a similar foul ball left Tucker with a right shin fracture that sidelined him for three months.
However, he said this one hit in a different spot of his leg, while once again downplaying the potential severity of the problem.
“This was a little different,” he said. “I feel fine.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers kept right fielder Kyle Tucker out of their lineup for Sunday’s game after he exited Saturday’s win early.
Tucker fouled a ball off of his shin Saturday, and left the game shortly after. Manager Dave Roberts expected Tucker to return to the lineup Sunday, but the outfielder clearly isn’t fit to participate.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers are running a bullpen day on Sunday, and could have a few players fill in if needed. Jack Dreyer is getting the ball first for the Dodgers, making his second start of the season. He has a 3.19 ERA through 63 appearances with 68 strikeouts in 59.1 innings pitched.
Emmet Sheehan has a locker at Dodger Stadium as well, and could handle bulk for LA on Sunday.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
Shortstop Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot for the Dodgers, and center fielder Tommy Edman shoots up the order to bat second. Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez bats third, and first baseman Freddie Freeman serves as the cleanup hitter.
Miguel Rojas enters the lineup as the second baseman and No. 5 hitter, and third baseman Max Muncy slides down the order to the No. 6 spot. Josue De Paula remains the team’s designated hitter, and following him are left fielder Kiké Hernandez and catcher Hunter Feduccia to round out the Dodgers’ lineup.
Dodgers Lineup vs. Giants
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Tommy Edman, CF
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Freddie Freeman, 1B
5. Miguel Rojas, 2B
6. Max Muncy, 3B
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Kiké Hernandez, LF
9. Hunter Feduccia, C
Who is Starting for the Giants?
On the mound for the Giants is left-hander Matt WIlkinson, who will be making his seventh appearance of the year. He has a 4.58 ERA through 19.2 innings pitched, striking out 12 batters durign that time.
The rookie struggled in his first stint as a starter, transitioning to relief for his last two appearances and holding his opponents scoreless.
The Dodgers will look to break his scoreless streak in Sunday’s game, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Scout's Josue De Paula assessment will excite Dodgers fans
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers might have their next homegrown superstar in outfielder Josue De Paula. That's at least according to one National League scout who spoke with FanSided. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers might have their next homegrown superstar in outfielder Josue De Paula. That's at least according to one National League scout who spoke with FanSided.
"JDP is the most polished young hitter I have seen in my 17 years of professional baseball," the scout said. "He is never rushed, immensely confident, and has been incredibly consistent since entering pro ball."
De Paula has done nothing but produce in the minor leagues since signing with the Dodgers out of the Dominican Republic as a 16-year-old in 2022. This season, he slashed .303/.401/.547 with a .948 OPS, 27 homers, 104 RBI and 31 stolen bases in 124 games in Double-A. As a result, he replaced Shohei Ohtani, who went on the IL with knee and biceps injuries, on the Dodgers' roster this month.
De Paula, 21, was called up to make his MLB debut on September 11. He proceeded to crush a moonshot of a three-run home run two days later for his first career big league hit. The future is certainly bright for the left-handed hitter. De Paula is the Dodgers' No. 1 ranked prospect and No. 4 in all of baseball, per Baseball America.
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula was compared to MLB legend Manny Ramirez
The same scout told FanSided that De Paula's natural hitting skills compare to a former Dodger and legendary slugger.
"The only fair comparison to the ease in which hitting comes to (De Paula) is Manny Ramirez," the scout said. "He was born to hit and has done nothing but refine his gift the last four-plus years."
This is good company to be in. Ramirez was a 12-time All-Star and nine-time Silver Slugger Award winner across 18-years in the big leagues. He led the American League in RBI (1999), won a batting title (2002) and led the AL in home runs (2004). Ramirez was also a two-time World Series champion with the Boston Red Sox and won World Series MVP in 2004. Ramirez would be in the Hall of Fame if not for his ties to performance-enhancing drugs.
If De Paula can have similar results in the majors as Ramirez, the youngster will be in pretty good shape, and so will the Dodgers. Los Angeles has center fielder Andy Pages under control through 2030, left fielder Teoscar Hernandez is entering the final year of his deal in 2027, and Kyle Tucker is in year-one of a four-year, $240 million deal that has opt outs after 2027 and 2028. Luckily, De Paula is expected to be a future core piece of the Dodgers' outfield for many years to come.

item.title: [pasadenastarnews.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
Mookie Betts had four hits, including three doubles, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4
LOS ANGELES -- Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning.
Every Dodger had at least one hit, except for struggling Freddie Freeman who was 0 for 5. Betts tied his season high for hits and the team outslugged the Giants, 15-8. The former AL MVP was hitting .249 a week ago, and has since raised his average to .261.
The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.
The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.
Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.
Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third.
Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal (11-7) wasn't particularly sharp, allowing four runs and eight hits in five innings. The left-hander struck out three and walked two, with the Dodgers winning each of his last six outings.
Reliever Edwin Díaz pitched a scoreless eighth in his second straight appearance since coming off the injured list Friday.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.
Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker fouled a ball off his knee and was replaced by Alex Call in the seventh.
Neither team had announced their starters for the series finale Sunday.

item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky

After Tarik Skubal allowed a two-out walk to Giants designated hitter Victor Bericoto, Jung Hoo Lee attacked the first pitch he saw into the right-center field gap, but a diving play from Kyle Tucker got Skubal out of the inning with the game remaining scoreless. item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers and San Francisco Giants kept things neck-and-neck through the first half of Saturday night’s contest, but the Dodgers rattled off six unanswered runs in a 10-4 victory.
After Tarik Skubal allowed a two-out walk to Giants designated hitter Victor Bericoto, Jung Hoo Lee attacked the first pitch he saw into the right-center field gap, but a diving play from Kyle Tucker got Skubal out of the inning with the game remaining scoreless.
Mookie Betts started things off in the bottom of the first inning with a leadoff double, and Max Muncy cashed him in with a two-strike, two-out RBI double to give the Dodgers the first lead of the game. Betts would come through again in the bottom of the second inning, lacing an RBI single the other way to plate Josue De Paula and make it a 2-0 Dodger lead.
Skubal worked his way around two baserunners for a scoreless top of the second inning, but after allowing a one-out single to Turner Hill in the top of the third inning, Bericoto launched a 3-2 fastball deep over the center field wall, tying the game at 2. Will Smith wasted no time giving the Dodgers the lead again, hammering a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the third inning, giving him his second home run in as many games.
The Giants responded with a pair of leadoff singles from Andrew Knizner and Osleivis Basabe to begin the top of the fourth inning. A bunt from Christian Koss moved both men into scoring position, and a squeeze bunt from Jonah Cox plated Knizner to tie the game at 3.
The Dodgers would get another one-run lead thanks to an RBI double from Mookie Betts in the bottom of the fourth inning— his second double and second RBI of the game. The Giants wouldn’t let Skubal settle in for the top of the fifth inning, as Bericoto and Lee both doubled to tie the game at four.
Saturday turned out to be Skubal’s worst outing of the season, let alone as a Dodger. Skubal managed to complete five innings of work but allowed a season-high four earned runs, while his three strikeouts on the night were the fewest in any start since striking out three on August 14 of last season against the Minnesota Twins.
Despite the poor start, the Dodgers put Skubal officially in line for the win as Teoscar Hernández ignited a two-out rally with an opposite-field single. Kyle Tucker and Josue De Paula each followed with a walk, and Tommy Edman snapped out of a 1-37 funk with a go-ahead, two-run single to give the Dodgers their first multi-run lead since the third. Miguel Rojas knocked a pinch-hit single to bring home De Paula, but Edman was thrown out at home attempting to make it a four-run inning.
Evan Phillips recorded the first clean inning of the night in relief of Skubal in the top of the sixth inning, and the Dodgers responded with another three-run inning, capitalized by a two-run single by De Paula and giving the Dodgers a six-run cushion.
After a scoreless inning from Alex Vesia in the seventh inning, Edwin Díaz came in for his second consecutive game since returning from injury, pitching a scoreless top of the eighth inning while picking up a pair of strikeouts.
Mookie Betts finished Saturday going 4-4 with three doubles and two RBI, reaching base five times after a walk in the seventh inning. Betts is now 10-12 (.833 average) over his last three games with three doubles, two home runs and five RBI.
With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintain a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the no. 2 seed in the National League. They still trail the Milwaukee Brewers by two games for the top seed.
Game particulars
- Home runs— Victor Bericoto (5); Will Smith (9)
- WP— Tarik Skubal (11-7): 5 IP, 8 hits, 4 earned runs, 2 walks, 3 strikeouts
- LP— Yunior Marte (0-1): 4 2/3 IP, 8 hits, 6 earned runs, 3 walks, 2 strikeouts
Up next
The Dodgers wrap things up against San Francisco on Sunday (1:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before hosting the San Diego Padres for their final regular season home series beginning Tuesday. Both teams have yet to announce their starters.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers' September surge continues: L.A. racks up 15 hits in win over Giants
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants. When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense. In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense.
In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies in back-to-back innings to take pressure off the pitching staff.
Before that breakout started in the fifth inning, it was a back-and-forth game.
Dodgers left-handed starting pitcher Tarik Skubal pitched only five innings, tied for his shortest start with the Dodgers. And he surrendered four runs, the worst mark of his Dodgers tenure.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
Entering the game, Skubal appeared to be peaking. His last two starts, both against the Reds, were some of his most efficient.
That efficiency, however, regressed against the Giants (64-91).
Though he got through the first two innings without giving up a run — thanks in part to a diving catch by right fielder Kyle Tucker made in the gap to end the first — he issued two-out walks in each.
The Dodgers’ offense used that time to mount a lead. Leadoff hitter Mookie Betts, who finished the day with three doubles and a single, hit the first of those doubles in his first at-bat, and Max Muncy authored his own to drive in the first run.
The next inning, rookie Josue De Paula’s walk, and singles from Alex Freeland and Betts combined to push in another run.
Then Skubal began to struggle. With a runner on second and one out, he pitched to a full count against designated hitter Victor Bericoto. Skubal missed down the middle with a fastball, and Bericoto sent it 425 feet to center field. It landed on the netting on the other side of the wall to tie the score.
The Dodgers’ offense, coming alive in September, struck back in the third. Catcher Will Smith hit his second home run in as many nights, launching the second pitch of the frame into left-field stands.
The Giants took a different approach to tie the score for a second time. After back-to-back singles, they used back-to-back sacrifice bunts to advance the runners and score another run.
Then the two teams traded runs again. Betts put the Dodgers (95-60) up with an RBI double in the fourth. Skubal gave up back-to-back doubles in the fifth.
That marked both the end of Skubal’s start and the beginning of the Dodgers’ offensive onslaught.
If the man trying to revive the Montreal Expos as an expansion team succeeds, Dan Evans is his choice for president of baseball operations.
The Dodgers brought seven batters to the plate in the fifth, and all but one reached base. Tommy Edman hit a two-run single. And pinch-hitting Miguel Rojas almost matched him, but Giants left fielder Turner Hill made a perfect throw to nab Edman in a close play at home to end the inning.
Betts’ and Smith’s bats stayed hot to open the sixth with a leadoff double and one-out RBI single, respectively. The Dodgers took advantage of the Giants’ sloppy infield play to load the bases for De Paula, who lined a two-run single into shallow center field.
Those were the kinds of stifling rallies that had defined the Dodgers offense earlier in the season, when they were scoring regularly in double digits.
The Dodgers’ 15 hits Saturday were their most in a game since July 2 against the San Diego Padres, and just two shy of their season high.

item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker left the game Saturday, Sept. 19th, against the San Francisco Giants after fouling a pitch off his right knee. Tucker, in his last at-bat, swung at a pitch and the ball landed on the inside of his knee. Kyle Tucker exited early Saturday after fouling off a pitch off his right knee. On the Spectrum broadcast, David Vassegh said he spoke with the trainer, and the move was precautionary, with the score factored in as well. pic.twitter.com/s95AOopR9P On th
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker left the game Saturday, Sept. 19th, against the San Francisco Giants after fouling a pitch off his right knee.
Tucker, in his last at-bat, swung at a pitch and the ball landed on the inside of his knee.
Kyle Tucker exited early Saturday after fouling off a pitch off his right knee.
On the Spectrum broadcast, David Vassegh said he spoke with the trainer, and the move was precautionary, with the score factored in as well. pic.twitter.com/s95AOopR9P
On the Spectrum broadcast, he was seen favoring it, and while he played defense for an inning, he was later removed from the game.
"Considering the score, the feeling I'm getting from the dugout, Dodgers trainer Thomas Albert saying, 'Obviously, just playing it safe,'" Vassegh said on the broadcast.
As Vassegh noted, Tucker was indeed smiling while in the dugout, sitting on the bench, still favoring the knee a bit.
All indicators suggest the move was to preserve Tucker, especially with the postseason around the corner, rather than push things.
Tucker was 1-for-3 with a walk and an RBI before getting yanked, another marker of his recent surge at the plate.
Given how much he uses his right leg to rotate, it will be important to monitor whether his swing changes at all.
Kyle Tucker's hot streak
Over his last 15 games, Tucker is hitting .327/.424/.796 with six home runs and 12 RBIs, with just nine walks and six punchouts, per MLB.com.
Over his last seven games, things look even better: .391/.533/.870.
All of this offensive success is thanks to meaningful mechanical tweaks.
"Right now he's in a great spot mechanically," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation. "Now with the confidence that he has with his swing … it has happened quickly.
"I know that the hitting coach has kind of unlocked something with Kyle, and it's just good to see it translate that quickly. Because most of the time, things like that take a while — you know, 15, 20, at-bats — but it kind of happened overnight with the results. So, really happy to see that."

According to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya, Pages was facing velocity off the machine at Dodger Stadium on Saturday. He may still have to face live pitching before the Do
item.content:encoded:
Andy Pages has been out with a left-hand fracture and has not played since Aug. 21.
The Dodgers recently revealed that they plan to activate him on the final homestand of the season, which started on Friday. While Pages did not make his return in the opener and is not in the lineup on Saturday, he is making significant progress.
According to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya, Pages was facing velocity off the machine at Dodger Stadium on Saturday. He may still have to face live pitching before the Dodgers activate him, but the fact that he is facing velocity is a good sign.
It's possible that the Dodgers activate him in the San Diego Padres series. The Padres are trying to clinch a spot in the postseason, and the Dodgers are their final opponent before what could be a very important series against the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Pages was an All-Star this year, slashing .272/.338/.797 with 21 home runs. Kyle Tucker, Teoscar Hernández and Mookie Betts are starting to get hot, and adding Pages back into the mix could make the Dodgers the threat every fan expected them to be in the offseason.
The Dodgers have been one of the best teams in baseball this year, but overall, some of their stars have been disappointing. Tucker has struggled for most of the year, and Betts did not look like himself for much of the season. However, things are starting to click in time for October.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are hoping to keep the momentum rolling after an electric series-opening win against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers won 8-2 on Friday night at Dodger Stadium, their first game back from a seven-game road trip. Many struggling Dodgers got a notable confidence boost, and the hope is that it carries over.
Dodgers’ Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Will Smith, C
4. Max Muncy, 3B
5. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
6. Kyle Tucker, RF
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Tommy Edman, CF
9. Alex Freeland, 2B
On Friday, Kyle Tucker went 2-for-3 with a home run and a walk. Over the last seven games, he is raking: .333/.467/.792 through seven games with three home runs, six walks, and just three strikeouts.
Additionally, Mookie Betts is red-hot. Over his last 15 games, he is hitting .356/.457/.729, according to MLB.com.
The Dodgers are facing a righty, but for Betts, it has not mattered what hand the pitcher uses.
Tucker could use another good game to keep the ball rolling, but really, Freddie Freeman is the name to watch.
He is still in a slump, and as he battles a knee injury, Freeman will be worth monitoring.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers have Tarik Skubal on the mound, making his penultimate regular-season start as a Dodger.
Skubal has really started rounding into form. He has a 2.52 ERA through eight games in blue, with just 57 strikeouts and 11 walks.
The stuff for Skubal still hasn’t reached its former peak, but his last start was a real taste of what he brings. He pitched seven innings, allowed 1 walk, three hits, and totaled nine strikeouts.
Skubal is building toward a classic Skubal outing, looking unhittable through every pitch.

item.content:encoded:
‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles
When the Los Angeles Dodgers were in Cincinnati on the second leg of their most recent road trip, manager Dave Roberts approached Josue De Paula.
"Just wait until we get back to LA," he recalled Roberts telling him. "It's different."
Sure enough, the raucous 48,000 fans -- a light crowd by Dodger Stadium standards -- packed inside Chavez Ravine for his home debut on Friday, Sept. 18 surpassed whatever the rookie's expectations were. Everything, from the environment to the deafening cheers that only seemed to grow louder as the Dodgers slugged their way to an 8-2 win over the hated rival San Francisco Giants, to the air itself, felt different.
"It's like a movie, man," De Paula told USA TODAY Sports.
De Paula, 21, has played his role perfectly through his first week in the big leagues.
The No. 6 prospect in baseball carries himself with a confidence that's rarely seen in someone as young as him. He's played in only eight games since being called up straight from Double-A Tulsa after Shohei Ohtani was placed on the injured list, or "just thrown into it" as he put it, but De Paula has relied on the skillset that got him here. He controls the strike zone, seeing the ball extremely well and is selective with what pitches he swings at, rarely chasing. That part of his game has transitioned seamlessly.
When De Paula does see a pitch he likes, his calm demeanor at the plate helps him stay centered and keeps him from jumping out ahead of the ball.
"I feel the adrenaline, but I feel like I just know how to pinpoint it and focus it," he said. "I'm so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down."
And when he does make contact, it's loud. So is De Paula.
That was seen in the bottom of the sixth inning on Friday. De Paula walked up to "Ima Boss" by Meek Mill (his third different walk-up song of the night by the way, this one was chosen by his mom). The triumphant horns on the 2011 anthem produced by Jahlil Beats had barely subsided over the loudspeakers when De Paula slapped a first-pitch slider from Giants reliever Jason Foley 107 mph into the gap in the right field for an RBI double that scored the go-ahead run from first.
Once he got to second base standing up, De Paula threw his hands in the air and hit the Dodgers' on-base celebration, swiveling his hips around before putting his own twist on it: pounding his chest and flexing toward his teammates in the dugout.
"He loves playing the game," Mookie Betts said. "He's full of life. When he gets on the field, it's like a quiet focus, but when he's off the field he likes joking ... and whatnot. He's a good kid."
Where does that unflappable joy come from?
"We got some swag in Brooklyn. We got some swag in the Dominican Republic. I just feel like I got a chip on my shoulder," De Paula said. "And it just comes out naturally."
That came out again in the bottom of the eighth when Giants reliever Philip Abner threw a first-pitch fastball up that was called a strike by umpire Louie Krupa. De Paula immediately tapped his helmet to challenge, and ABS showed the ball had missed the top of the zone 0.1 inches. The Dodger Stadium crowd got fired up as they watched the replay unfold on the jumbotron and the call was overturned to ball one, and De Paula nodded his head toward his teammates before working a two-out walk on four pitches.
Betts homered in the very next at-bat to break open a five-run lead. Will Smith then followed that up with the Dodgers' fourth long ball of the inning.
"Love De Paula," Roberts said. "I just love his at-bats. It's one of those things that we knew that coming up to the big leagues, he wasn't going to get overwhelmed, and it just helps when you control the strike zone. He takes his walks, when the ball is in the hitting zone, he can slug you, but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."
De Paula finished his Dodger Stadium debut 2-for-3 with two runs, and RBI and a walk to bring his OPS up to .924. It's been a very small sample size, and baseball has a way of humbling even the most skilled hitters. It is, after all, a game of failure. But what he has been able to do in his first "trial run", filling in for the back-to-back National League MVP no less, might be indicative of something larger.
At the very least, he's played himself into the postseason roster conversation.
"To have (Roberts) believe in me so much," De Paula said. "I always have confidence in myself but to have someone like that believe in you, it just puts another oomph on your shoulder. It feels amazing."
For now, De Paula's just working. The weakest area of his game is his defense, and while the vast majority of this first stint in the majors will be as a designated hitter, he's using the opportunity get better. De Paula's taking advice from Roberts and the entire coaching staff. He's asking his teammates questions. He's shagging fly balls every day.
"I'm gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon," he said. "It's gonna take some time."
That opportunity likely won't come for a while; Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker are both getting hot and settling into their rhythms in the corner outfield spots in the final two weeks of the regular season. If De Paula does make the postseason roster after Ohtani comes back, it would probably be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Whatever happens over the next two weeks before October, De Paula's focused on the now, enjoying every moment he can. He got the ball back from his first Dodger Stadium hit – a leadoff single to right field in the fifth inning – and he knows exactly where to put it.
"I'm gonna give it to my parents," De Paula said. "I might give it to them right now."

item.title: [MARCA] Ohtani ramps up hitting progression: Why Dave Roberts is bullish on star's October return
item.dc:creator: Adriano Boin
item.description: - Los Angeles Dodgers. Dodgers facing nightmare playoff decision over Edwin Díaz as October looms - Los Angeles Dodgers. “They basically lie”: Shohei Ohtani accused of hiding multiple injuries to avoid being placed on Dodgers' injured list Shohei Ohtani’s path back to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup is becoming clearer, and manager Dave Roberts has provided another encouraging sign as the club prepares for October.
